A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Interaction Field Matching work. All pages, including Appendices A–B, are readable, and the text, equations, figures, and tables support matching retained content across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian transfer experiments and colored-MNIST generation and translation results in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 reports original toy experiments, image generation and translation results, quantitative benchmark comparisons, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 changes the stated regression target from the raw field to its normalized direction (v1 Equation 13; v2 Equation 11). Appendix A.2 also introduces explicit probabilistic stopping at successive plate crossings for the general transport maps. These revise training and general inference, although the concrete field construction is retained. v2 Algorithm 1 still displays the old loss, leaving the implemented objective unclear.

E1.justification: v2 replaces colored-MNIST generation with CIFAR-10 32×32 and CelebA 64×64 generation, and adds Winter-to-Summer 64×64 translation. Colored-MNIST 2-to-3 translation and the Gaussian toy scenarios remain. This substantially broadens coverage to natural objects, faces, and seasonal scenes.

E2.justification: Generation comparisons expand from EFM and PFGM to include PFGM++, FM, DDPM, and StyleGAN. Translation comparisons expand from EFM to include FM, CycleGAN, and DDIB. These methods participate in v2 Figures 9–10 and Tables 1–2, rather than appearing only as citations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces FID evaluation for generation and CMMD evaluation for translation, replacing exclusively qualitative image comparisons. For retained MNIST translation, the reported batch size changes from 64 to 128 and plate distance from 10 to 20. Appendix B also introduces an inference-time protocol across five batch sizes, with reported shared architecture, solver, and inference-step controls.

E4.justification: The Gaussian plate-distance sensitivity illustration is retained. Independent versus minibatch-OT coupling comparisons gain quantitative evidence and extend to Winter-to-Summer translation. Appendix B adds a limited computational analysis of inference time versus batch size and peak memory usage.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new numerical tables in v2 report individual values without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive numerical and qualitative results. Table 1 reports IFM FIDs of 2.28 on CIFAR-10 and 3.07 on CelebA, versus PFGM++ values of 2.15 and 2.89; EFM exceeds 100 on CelebA. Table 2 reports IFM-MB CMMD values of 0.87 for digit translation and 1.13 for Winter-to-Summer. Table 4 adds timing measurements. MNIST generation examples disappear, and translation examples are replaced under revised settings.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly requires unit-pair total flux to be independent of particle separation and states regularity assumptions for exchanging integrals. Appendix A.2 defines stopping probabilities, and v1's line-termination assumption becomes Lemma A.6 with a proof. The main theorem derivation is also revised. These are substantive mathematical changes, although v2 Equations 33–34 and 47 omit flux-normalization factors present in surrounding statements.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements, and discussion retain the same central claims: IFM generalizes EFM, a quark-inspired field avoids backward trajectories and plate-exit problems, and transport plans can influence the mapping. The expanded experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes that independent-plan translation fails to preserve content or style, whereas v2 describes both IFM variants as preserving shapes, with a modest advantage for minibatch OT. Appendix B newly attributes equal inference times to shared computational settings. The discussion's numerical-precision limitation and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 expands Appendix B with benchmark hyperparameters, shared architecture and solver disclosures, memory information, and additional baseline code sources and DDPM parameters. Reported training hardware changes from GTX 1080 Ti to A100. Section 3.5 newly specifies uniform coordinate sampling. Existing Adam, EMA, and learning-rate warmup details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for StyleGAN, CycleGAN, and the stated CMMD evaluation, while removing background references including Ehrenfest, Gurevich–Mostepanenko, and Gushchin et al. The central positioning relative to EFM, PFGM, and flow matching remains. The added Yan et al. reference is titled as a root-cause-analysis work, leaving its relevance to image evaluation unclear.

P1.justification: v2 swaps the generation and translation subsections, moves and expands the stochastic-map definition into Appendix A.2, and edits method explanations, cross-references, author information, and citation style. Most of the abstract, introduction, background, and discussion retains its wording and narrative.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, title block, headings, and page layout, moves Figure 1 onto the first page, and reflows figures and algorithms. Image results become larger comparisons spanning multiple datasets and methods. New FID, CMMD, and timing tables accompany an expanded hyperparameter table, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Natural-image FID comparisons provide stronger evidence of practical applicability than v1's qualitative digit demonstrations, and the explicit stopping construction fills a gap in the transport description. These gains are tempered by conflicting loss specifications, inconsistent flux normalization in revised proofs, and an inadequately identified CMMD metric. The additions improve the paper, but these reporting problems limit the strength of the overall gain.
